title: A googol got its name from a nine-year-old
body: In 1920 mathematician Edward Kasner asked his nephew Milton Sirotta to name 10^100; the child said 'googol'. Kasner's book popularised googol and googolplex, giving English handles for numbers beyond any counting need. A search company later chose a misspelling of it as a name, preferring the accident to the original.
source_hint: Kasner and Newman, 'Mathematics and the Imagination' (1940)
